title: Belinda Peter
text:
I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Political Science at Temple University a comparativist whose research focuses on India. My research interest lies at the intersection of political communication and political behavior. My work examines a central question arising from the current era of democratic backsliding: Do voters recognize democratic backsliding as a threat, understand its consequences, and act to hold politicians accountable?
I approach this question by examining the full chain through which democratic backsliding becomes, or fails to become, politically consequential. I use survey experiments and causal inference to understand how voters respond when they encounter information about departures from democratic norms. I also analyze media environments using large language models (LLMs) and machine learning to examine how information about democratic backsliding is communicated to the public, particularly whether procedural and technical reporting obscures political responsibility and fails to convey the urgency of democratic erosion. Together, these approaches allow me to examine how democratic backsliding is communicated, how voters interpret it, and whether that understanding translates into political accountability.
Prior to Temple University, I worked as Teacher in Jammu and Kashmir, India and taught as an adjunct faculty at Stella Maris College, Chennai India.
